National reporting-polygon layers

Source: R/reportingPolygons.R
nationalReportingLayers.Rd

Layers for summarising a simulation by jurisdiction and by national ecological and conservation units, rather than by forest tenure: provinces and territories, ecozones (the row of reportingPolygonLayers()), terrestrial protected areas, the federal boreal caribou ranges, and intact forest. None is crossed with a tenure. Pass the rows wanted as layers to buildReportingPolygons().

nationalReportingLayers()

Value

A tibble with the columns of reportingPolygonLayers(), query, layer, dissolve and labelMap.

Details

  • Province: NRCan's CanVec 1:1,000,000 administrative boundaries (geo_political_region_2, Open Government Licence - Canada), named by two-letter code (AB, BC, ..., YT) through labelMap, and dissolved to one feature per province or territory. Not GADM, whose licence bars commercial use and redistribution without permission, nor Statistics Canada's boundary file (lpr_000b21a_e.zip), which answers scripted downloads with a browser check (HTTP 403).

  • Protected: the Canadian Protected and Conserved Areas Database (CPCAD, ECCC, 2025), terrestrial protected areas only (PA_OECM_DF = 1, BIOME = 'T'; OECMs and interim areas excluded). Every feature is labelled "Protected", so the layer is one reporting unit: all protected land in the study area, dissolved so that overlapping areas count once.

  • BorealCaribou: ECCC's 51 boreal caribou ranges (2012 boundaries), the ranges of the federal recovery strategy and its 35% disturbance threshold, named by HERD. The Caribou layer of reportingPolygonLayers() is the jurisdictional ranges instead.

  • Intact: the Intact Forest Landscapes of 2025 (Potapov et al. 2017, Science Advances 3:e1600821; https://intactforests.org, CC BY 4.0, so outputs that use it must credit it): forest and natural treeless land (tundra, wetlands, rock) in patches of at least 500 km2 with no detectable industrial use (roads, logging, mining), as one reporting unit, "Intact". It stands in for primary forest, which no national map shows, but it maps intactness, not forest: it includes non-forest land and leaves out unlogged areas under 500 km2. The forest inside it comes from the vegetation maps.

  • Intact2000: the same for 2000, the first year mapped, as one unit, "Intact2000". With Intact, it gives the loss of intact forest since 2000: land no longer intact, which includes landscapes split by roads or other industrial use below the IFL size and width thresholds, not only forest cover lost.

query is an OGR SQL query read with the source; it names the layer of a multi-layer source. layer names the file to read when a download holds several (CanVec's holds one shapefile per feature type). dissolve = TRUE merges each unit's features into one, so overlaps count once. labelMap renames source labels to unit names (CanVec's English names to two-letter codes).
